subject: Hosted inference: Partial-generation truncation window — immediate notice
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Wong <emma.wong@citrinelabs.com>, ops@citrinelabs.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted inference: Partial-generation truncation window — immediate notice

Hi Emma / Citrine Ops team,

I wanted to let you know we observed a short window of partial-generation truncation affecting streaming responses for some requests to the hosted-generation endpoint (model: rdx-gpt-large-v2) earlier today. The window was from 2026-12-20T07:59:20Z to 2026-12-20T08:13:05Z (approximately 14 minutes). During that time some streaming sessions were cut short and returned a final token earlier than expected.

What we know so far:
- Scope: ~0.4% of requests hitting the streaming path for that model variant in us-west-1.
- User-visible impact: truncated outputs (early termination) or incomplete streamed chunks for sessions using the streaming API. No wrong-text generation reported.
- Immediate mitigation: automatic fallback to the non-streaming generation path was enabled at 08:04 PST for requests that matched the failure signature; traffic was gradually routed back to the normal path starting 08:10 PST as we validated fixes.

Next steps we are taking (short term):
1) We captured detailed KV cache eviction traces and request logs for the window and attached a short digest.
2) We rolled a targeted rollback of a microkernel change to the KV eviction heuristics to restore previous behavior.
3) We are running graduated traffic tests across replicas to confirm stability; we expect normal behavior to be fully validated by 09:00 PST.

What we need from you
- If you have examples or request IDs from affected calls, please reply with those (request ids or timestamps) and we’ll prioritize them in the impact analysis.

Status & links
- Status page incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-12020-kv-evict
- Internal investigation ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721

Attachments: kv-eviction-log-20261220.txt (text/plain) — brief traces and sampling; customer-impact-digest.pdf (application/pdf) — short summary for ops teams.

Apologies for the disruption — we know streaming is integral to your workflow. I’ll follow up with a short timeline and permanent remediation plan once we complete the initial RCA.

Warmly,
Irene Choi
Senior Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — appreciate the heads up. Two quick questions:
1) Did this affect the incremental chunking for our live-transcription flow or only batch streaming? We saw a few sessions with missing final sentences around 08:05 PST.
2) Is there a flag we can set client-side to avoid the fallback (we want to prefer complete streaming even if slightly delayed)?

I can pull a few example request ids if it helps; we’re checking our logs now.

—Emma

Head of Platform Engineering, Citrine Labs
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:05:12-08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted inference: Partial-generation truncation window — immediate notice

Quick internal note / suggestion:
- Root cause signal: correlated spike in KV eviction loop iterations after the microkernel change (see INF-4721). Eviction policy started evicting prefix entries prematurely under a hot-prefix pattern, which caused the streaming path to return early when KV cache was missing.
- Mitigation already applied: rolled the microkernel change on the affected pool and engaged prefix warming to reduce cache misses.
- Proposed follow-up: schedule a 60-minute postmortem with infra + runtime + QA to capture timeline and cover rollout gating for kernel changes. I’ll attach the sampled flame traces to the ticket.

Action items I recommend for customer comms:
1) Provide a short timeline and confirmation when full validation completes (Irene).
2) Offer guidance for client-side resiliency (retry/backoff and idempotency tokens) and an optional SDK flag to prefer full stream semantics over fallback (Lauren + SDK).
3) Prepare a brief credit offer for impacted token usage (we should run an impact calc once Emma provides request ids).

Irene — want to coordinate the postmortem invite now? I can book INF on the calendar at 10:30 PST.

—Aditya
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Wong <emma.wong@citrinelabs.com>, ops@citrinelabs.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T12:35:00-08:00
Subject: Update & follow-up: Timeline, mitigation, and next steps (Post-incident summary)

Hi Emma — thanks for the quick reply and for pulling logs. We completed the initial validation and wanted to share a concise post-incident summary and the concrete next steps.

Incident timeline (UTC):
- 2026-12-20T07:59:20Z — first anomalous truncation observed in streaming path; automated alert triggered.
- 2026-12-20T08:02:34Z — rollback of the microkernel change initiated for the impacted pool.
- 2026-12-20T08:04:12Z — automatic fallback enabled for requests that matched failure signature (to minimize customer-visible truncation).
- 2026-12-20T08:10:55Z — progressive traffic validation across replicas; fallback gradually removed for validated nodes.
- 2026-12-20T08:13:05Z — normal streaming behavior restored for all monitored nodes.

Root cause (summary):
- A recent microkernel change to the KV eviction heuristic caused higher-than-expected eviction of active prefix entries under a hot-prefix workload. When the KV cache missed at certain points during streaming, the runtime returned early (finalization) rather than waiting or re-fetching the prefix, which produced truncated streamed outputs.

Actions taken (short & long term):
Short term:
- Rolled kernel change for affected pool and enabled prefix warming for hot sessions.
- Added more conservative eviction thresholds for the next 3 rollout waves.

Planned long-term mitigations:
- Add a streaming-path guard that will prefer rehydration of the KV prefix over early finalization for in-flight sessions.
- Improve rollout gating and automated canary checks for microkernel changes (INF-4721).
- SDK update: optional flag to prefer full streaming semantics (work scheduled with SDK team; ETA early Q1).

Customer impact & compensation
- Based on our sampling, Citrine Labs saw ~0.35% of streaming requests truncated during the window. We will produce a precise impacted token count after you share request IDs or samples; I will follow up with a recommended usage credit.

Next steps / asks
1) If you can share 3–5 example request IDs or timestamps where you saw truncated outputs, we’ll prioritize those for the deep dive.
2) I’ve scheduled a 60-minute postmortem at 2026-12-20T18:30:00Z (10:30 PST) with infra/runtime/QA; invite link: https://calendly.com/irene-choi/redwood-postmortem. If you’d like a separate customer-facing run-through, we can set a 30-minute slot after the internal RCA.

Attachments included: kv-eviction-log-20261220.txt, customer-impact-digest.pdf
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-12020-kv-evict
Internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721

Again — apologies for the disruption. We’re treating this with high priority and will deliver the follow-up RCA.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
